children: New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Axis Bank on Saturday, October 17, reported a 38% year-on-year (YoY) jump in net profit to Rs.7,003 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs.5,089 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The private sector lender's earnings were supported by growth in net interest income and an improvement in asset quality.

Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, increased 12% YoY to Rs.15,371 crore. Net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.36% during the quarter and improved to 3.47% after excluding the impact of foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposits.
Operating profit grew 6% YoY to Rs.11,083 crore, while core operating profit rose 11% to Rs.10,998 crore. Other income declined 1% to Rs.6,531 crore, even as fee income advanced 6% to Rs.6,381 crore.

Commenting on the bank's performance, managing director and CEO Amitabh Chaudhry said Axis Bank continued to focus on digital payments, secure banking, AI-driven innovation and strategic partnerships to strengthen its customer offerings.

Axis Bank reported a year-on-year improvement in its asset quality, with the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio falling 30 basis points (bps) to 1.16% in Q2FY27. The net non-performing asset (NNPA) ratio declined 9 bps to 0.35%.

Gross slippages dropped to Rs.4,762 crore during the September quarter, compared with Rs.5,566 crore in the preceding quarter and Rs.5,696 crore a year earlier. The net slippage ratio also declined 30 bps YoY to 0.75%.

The lender's annualised net credit cost came in at 0.45%, marking a reduction of 28 bps year-on-year and 18 bps sequentially. Meanwhile, its provision coverage ratio remained stable at 70%, unchanged from both the previous quarter and the corresponding period last year.
Axis Bank set aside Rs.1,694 crore towards provisions and contingencies in Q2FY27, including Rs.1,564 crore in specific loan-loss provisions.

As of September 30, 2026, the bank had accumulated Rs.15,860 crore in provisions against standard assets and additional provisions outside those for non-performing assets (NPAs). These were over and above the NPA provisions accounted for in the calculation of its provision coverage ratio.
Axis Bank's advances expanded 23% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter to Rs.13.74 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026.
Retail lending increased 16% YoY to Rs.7.40 lakh crore, representing 54% of net advances. SME loans grew 25% to Rs.1.65 lakh crore, while corporate lending registered growth of 34%.

Total deposits rose 21% year-on-year and 6% sequentially to Rs.14.52 lakh crore on a month-end basis. Term deposits recorded 27% growth, while current account deposits increased 7% and savings account deposits advanced 12%.
The current account and savings account (CASA) ratio stood at 36%. The bank's cost of funds also declined by 8 bps from the year-ago period.

Axis Bank's capital adequacy ratio stood at 16.27% as of September 30, 2026, while its common equity tier-1 (CET-1) ratio was 14.61%. The bank added 23 bps to its CET-1 ratio during the first half of FY27.

In addition, the lender held Rs.8,006 crore in provisions over and above those reflected in its reported capital adequacy ratio. These additional provisions represented a capital cushion equivalent to approximately 49 bps.
For the first half of FY27, Axis Bank's net profit climbed 30% year-on-year to Rs.14,117 crore from Rs.10,896 crore in H1FY26.
NII increased 10% to Rs.30,018 crore, while fee income rose 6% to Rs.12,536 crore. Operating profit advanced 4% to Rs.22,742 crore from Rs.21,928 crore in the year-ago period.
Core operating profit grew 11% to Rs.22,120 crore compared with Rs.20,010 crore in H1FY26.
Axis Bank shares ended Friday's session, October 16, at Rs.1,290, up 0.16%, ahead of the Q2FY27 earnings announcement.
The stock has gained around 4% over the past month but has declined 1.5% over three months and 4.5% over six months. Over the past year, it has advanced approximately 8%.

On a year-to-date basis, Axis Bank shares have gained 1.2%, outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen 11.5% over the same period. The lender's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs.4.02 lakh crore.
Investors will track the bank's net interest margins, loan growth, deposit mobilisation and asset quality in assessing the sustainability of earnings growth and the stock's outlook.
